newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan eases foreign currency account restrictions.
newsitem.headline: Jordan eases foreign currency account restrictions.

text.p: Jordan's Central Bank has taken steps to allow banks to invest more of their foreign exchange holdings in international capital markets.
A circular to banks obtained by Reuters on Wednesday removes a ceiling equivalent to 500,000 dinars ($706,000) on foreign currency deposits Jordanians can hold in domestic banks.
It will also allow the banks to invest those foreign currency deposits in international capital markets and enter into foreign currency margin trading.
These were previously restricted to foreign currency accounts held by non-resident Jordanians.
Asset swap operations for Jordanian resident accounts would no longer need the approval of the Central Bank.
The rules should allow banks greater flexibility in investing surplus non-dinar funds, which prior to the move could only be placed in lower-yield eurodollar deposit markets.
Banks are already allowed to invest foreign currency holdings in Triple A rated international corporate bond issues and key government debt bonds with a maximum 10-year maturity.
Bankers say the new rules will allow banks to increase their profitability by investing in higher yield debt instruments and utilising more of their foreign currency holdings.
